reason: Cell junctions can connect the surface cells to begin forming the skin barrier.

reason: The tough outer layer has overlapping cells and lipids that could limit water loss from the connected sheet.

effect: The outer layer slows water loss, so the remaining skin pieces may provide support and touch sensing.
reaction: The comparison of water arrows makes the barrier's effect clear.
reason: The skin support cells and connective fibers appear to belong together in the supporting layer.

reaction: The tug panels help show how the fibers support the skin.
reason: The surface barrier and supporting layer appear to be complementary parts of the skin.
expectation: They will form a supported skin barrier.

reaction: The vessel inset clarifies where the skin's blood supply lies.
reason: The sensory endings are shown beneath a skin surface and should give the layered skin a way to detect contact.
expectation: The skin will gain touch-sensing nerve endings.

effect: The skin now senses contact, and the next goal is to connect it and the supply network to the arm.
reaction: The fingertip diagram makes the sensory endings' role clear.
reason: The sensitive skin can protect the working arm and provide contact information.
expectation: The arm will gain a protective, touch-sensitive covering.

effect: The arm now has a protective, touch-sensitive covering, but its vessels still need the body supply network.
reaction: The open vessel ends make the next connection clear.
reason: The body supply network can connect to the arm's vessels and provide continuing supplies.
expectation: The arm will connect to circulation and receive oxygen and nutrients.

reaction: The skin inset helps explain how cells receive supplies without blood cells leaving vessels.

effect: The final result shows how touch signals and muscle activity work together to steady the glass, completing the chapter.
reaction: The slipping-glass panels make the purpose of contact feedback clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Holding the glass was the most worthwhile action because it brought the skin, nerves and muscles together in a familiar task.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining the support cells and fibers was less engaging: the tug panels showed support, but the action itself was fairly predictable.

surprise.text: I was interested that the living surface cells receive supplies from vessels in the supporting layer while blood cells stay inside the vessels.

arbitrary.text: None of the combinations felt particularly arbitrary; the item descriptions and goals gave each a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would continue if another chapter connected the body systems to a different everyday problem. The glass sequence made their combined work more interesting than assembling layers alone.
